core_obligations: Record the common framework: tautness corresponds to representability, and both spaces are the filtered colimits of the spectra of the quotients of the two rings by weak ideals of definition, with the target's quotients the closures of the images of the source's (proof lines 6352-6358).

Direction from the ring-theoretic condition: choose a polynomial ring over the source with dense image in the target, observe that the induced maps on the quotients are surjective, and for a quasi-compact test scheme -- which factors through a quotient -- identify the base change of the morphism with a base change of a morphism of finite type between affine schemes (proof lines 6360-6374).

Direction from finite type: fix a weak ideal of definition and use the hypothesis to see that the corresponding map of quotients is of finite type, lift images of generators to the target ring, and show the resulting polynomial map has dense image (proof lines 6376-6381).

Complete the density argument: compare two quotients using that the closure of the image of the chosen ideal is cut out by an open ideal, and apply the criterion for surjectivity modulo a locally nilpotent ideal to get surjectivity of the polynomial map on the smaller quotient (proof lines 6381-6391).
proof_roadmap: Common framework: tautness as representability and the two colimit presentations (proof lines 6352-6358).
From topologically of finite type to finite type (proof lines 6360-6374).
From finite type to topologically of finite type: lifting generators (proof lines 6376-6381).
Density by comparing quotients and a surjectivity criterion (proof lines 6381-6391).
difficulty_reason: For a continuous map of weakly admissible topological rings over a scheme, the lemma states that the induced morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces is of finite type if and only if the ring map is taut and the target ring is topologically of finite type over the source (statement lines 6342-6350). The proof fixes a common framework: tautness corresponds to representability, and both spaces are written as filtered colimits of the spectra of their quotients by weak ideals of definition, the target's quotients being the closures of the images of the source's (proof lines 6352-6358). For the direction from the ring-theoretic condition, one chooses a ring map from a polynomial algebra with dense image, notes that it remains dense after passing to any of the quotients and hence is surjective there, and then for a quasi-compact test scheme over the source -- which factors through one of the quotients -- identifies the base change of the morphism with the base change of the corresponding map of affine schemes, which is of finite type (proof lines 6360-6374). For the converse one picks a quotient of the source, uses the hypothesis to see that the corresponding maps of quotients are of finite type, lifts images of generators back to the target ring, and shows the resulting polynomial map has dense image by comparing two quotients and applying the criterion for surjectivity modulo a locally nilpotent ideal (proof lines 6376-6391). The claim is H2: two implications are proved, each resting on a different observation -- the first on the compatibility of the presentations and the second on the comparison of two quotients through a surjectivity criterion.
